text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- 'After me the deluge', paper says in a reference to President Sali Berisha's bid to seek another term in office.
- Editorial says Berisha has definitely lost his credibility in the country as he has failed to persuade students not to start hunger strike.
- Two-page report on alleged violence by secret police against high schools students in Tirana, who tried to join University students in an attempt to start hunger strike.
- Thousands of students across the country have boycotted lectures in sign of support for Vlore and Gjirokaster students who have gone on hunger strike urging Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi to quit.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton meets an Albanian student studying in an American university, while Berisha tries to crack down on students protests, paper says.
- We want a realistic and uncensored television, state-run television trade union says in a statement which blamed the director for preventing reporters to tell the truth.
- Albania's economic situation is turning catastrophic, Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi is quoted as saying.
- Students in Elbasan town called on President Berisha not to seek a fresh term of office and urged Meksi to resign.
- After dramatic fall of the local currency, the lek, shopkeepers are beginning to sell their goods in U.S. dollars.
- Re-election of Berisha would deepen crisis which has hit Albania.
- Ruling Democratic Party is becoming an illegal party as it called on its supporters to enforce order, main opposition Forum for Democracy alliance says in a statement.
- The forum will hold rally in Tirana's main Skanderbeg square on Saturday.
- Parliament has announced it would hold a vote to elect the country's president on Monday. The Democratic Party chose President Sali Berisha as its candidate.
- Albanian government welcomes International Monetary Fund experts to help Albania get out of the crisis sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
